messages:
ashish: quick flag — dashboards are spiking when RBAC runs per-row. saw ~3x CPU on query-side and ~180-250ms extra latency per panel during peak; this is mostly on heavy tenant dashboards. thinking of an authz-sidecar that batches/checks a query shape and returns a compact allow-list + a version token, TTL ~5m. pros: avoids per-row calls and reduces DB auth pressure. cons: staleness on revokes, extra infra, cache invalidation complexity. thoughts? :thinking_face:

maya: which dashboards/queries specifically? is this only aggregate panels or the table views too?

ashish: mainly aggregate panels and some timeseries joins. example: 2M rows scanned but RBAC predicate applied row-by-row in the query engine (we call authz per-row in the current path). rough numbers from last load test attached: max_cpu 78% -> 240% (virtual across query fleet), p95 panel latency from 420ms -> 650ms.

ashish: rough sketch of sidecar response (pseudo):
```json
{
  "query_shape_id": "q_abc123",
  "allow_list": ["tenant:123:metric:read","tenant:123:meta:read"],
  "version_token": "v1.2026-03-12T12:00Z",
  "ttl_seconds": 300
}
```

liam: a couple things — how do you compute cache key? include subject_id + roles + query_shape_id? tenant isolation has to be strict. also size: allow_list for complex queries could be large and negate gains. any estimate on typical allow_list cardinality?

ashish: yes key = tenant_id + subject_roles_hash + query_shape_id. typical allow_list for dashboards we've seen is small (4-12 ACL entries) because panels mostly map to a handful of metrics/views. worst-case could be hundreds for ad-hoc tables though. we can cap response size and fall back to synchronous checks if >N entries.

sophia: operational concerns: invalidation is the killer. if an admin revokes a role, stale cache means a window of over-privilege. need strong invalidation: event-driven invalidation from IAM changes + a short TTL. also failure mode: if sidecar is down we must fail-safe (deny) or fall back to existing per-row checks? I lean fall back to per-row but with a circuit breaker so we don't regress fleet-wide.

liam: agree. event bus invalidation (kafka) with tombstone + local eviction works but adds complexity. another option: version_token tied to last-user-roles-change-seq for tenant; update when roles change. That keeps payloads tiny but still needs the same event plumbing.

maya: we also need telemetry: cache hit rate, avg allow_list size, staleness windows (time between role-change event and eviction), and any auth-falls to per-row path. if we can't measure safety, don't ship.

ashish: plan proposal: 1) spike implementation in staging sidecar, with conservative defaults (ttl=60s, max_allow_list_size=200), 2) rollout 1% of dashboard traffic -> 10% -> 50% with canary checks comparing results to current path, 3) event-driven invalidation prototype + fallback to per-row checks when mismatch/overflow. include metrics above.

maya: +1. please include rollout abort criteria (stale hits >1%, mismatch rate >0.1%, p95 regressions). also include security review sign-off path.

deploy-bot: staging | authz-sidecar-spike deployed to cluster staging-3 by ci-pipeline at 2026-03-12T15:02:13Z :rocket:

ashish: thanks — i'll draft an RFC and a small spike PR. assigning liam for cache key/invalidation design and sophia for failure-mode SLOs. will post link here when ready. :thumbsup:
